title: Explicit finite-prefix towers and their short exact augmentation
statement: Let $A:\mathbf N^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be a tower of abelian groups [def-weil-inverse-system, lem-pc-tower-abelian]. For $s\in\mathbf N$, define $T_s(A)_n=\prod_{i<n+s} A_i$, with restriction transitions and componentwise maps on tower morphisms. These give functors $T_s$. Define $i_A:A\to T_1(A)$ by $a\mapsto (f_{i,n}(a))_{i\le n}$, where $f_{i,n}:A_n\to A_i$ is the transition composite. Define $p_A:T_1(A)\to T_0(A)$ by $(x_i)\mapsto (x_i-f_{i,i+1}(x_{i+1}))_{i<n}$. They are natural in $A$, $p_A i_A=0$, and $0\to A\to T_1(A)\to T_0(A)\to0$ is short exact. Every successor transition of every $T_s(A)$ is surjective, also when $n+s=0$.

proof.text: Define finite products as dependent function groups on Fin(n+s). Restrict along every index morphism; identity and composition are pointwise identities. Apply tower morphisms coordinatewise. Define the augmentation by the transition composites and the difference by adjacent coordinates; tower naturality and functoriality of A show that these are natural transformations and that their composite is zero.

The last coordinate of the augmentation is the identity, hence it is injective. For a tuple in the kernel of the difference, reverse induction from the last coordinate gives x_i=f_{i,n}(x_n), so it is in the image. For a prescribed difference y, set x_n=0 and recurse downwards x_i=y_i+f_{i,i+1}(x_{i+1}); this proves surjectivity, including the empty target at n=0. Short exactness in the functor category follows by evaluation and the homology comparison isomorphism.
Extend a prefix by zero in the new coordinate to obtain a preimage under each successor transition. For an empty prefix this is the unique zero tuple.
